title: Outlook for Mac: Purview DLP policy tips with override
summary: Hold: the override configuration guidance omits Microsoft's requirement to set an appropriate BlockAccessScope as well as BlockAccess, which can leave administrators without a working override option. The roadmap facts, disabled default and Cloud Policy route are supported; licensing should distinguish published baseline DLP requirements from the unresolved Mac-specific advanced entitlement.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The override configuration guidance names BlockAccess true as the required check but omits the accompanying BlockAccessScope requirement.
claims.quote: If you set the NotifyAllowOverride action to WithoutJustification or WithJustification or FalsePositives, make sure BlockAccess is set to true and BlockAccessScope has appropriate value.
claims.fix: Add 'and BlockAccessScope has an appropriate value' to the BlockAccess requirement in controls[1].note, its rendered table note, Risk assessment and the At rollout checklist. Use: 'For an override option to appear, set BlockAccess to true and give BlockAccessScope an appropriate value, as Learn requires.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-use-notifications-and-policy-tips#user-override-support.

claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' for the published baseline DLP service requirement. Replace the opening licensing statement and notes with: 'The Purview service description licenses DLP for Exchange Online with plans including Microsoft 365 E3 and E5. It does not separately identify the advanced policy-tip entitlement for Outlook for Mac.' Retain the distinction from advanced Outlook for Microsoft 365 licensing, and narrow repeated statements that Learn lists no licences for Mac to this Mac-specific advanced entitlement gap. Cite the existing Purview service-description URL.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview route reaches the rule's Policy tips area through the oversharing walkthrough.
claims.quote: On the Define policy settings page, select Create or customize advanced DLP rules. ... Select Create rule. ... Set the User notifications toggle to On. ... Select Policy tips
claims.fix: The route stops on the right rule page rather than at the override option. For the cited oversharing walkthrough, the full labelled route is 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom > Admin units > Full directory > Exchange email > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User notifications > Policy tips > Show the policy tip as a dialog for the end user before send (available for Exchange workload only) > Allow override from M365 services'. Keep the explicit note that this is an oversharing walkthrough, not a Mac-specific route; do not describe its dialog selection as a requirement for basic Mac tips. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-osp-get-started.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <rule> -NotifyAllowOverride WithJustification modifies the identified DLP rule to allow override with justification.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the DLP rule that you want to modify. ... The NotifyAllowOverride parameter specifies the notification override options when the conditions of the rule are met. ... WithJustification: Allows overrides with justification.

claims.claim: The cited walkthrough names Allow override from M365 services as the rule's override checkbox and concerns oversharing in Outlook for Microsoft 365, not specifically Mac.
claims.quote: In Outlook for Microsoft 365, an oversharing pop-up displays a pop-up before a message is sent. ... If already selected, uncheck the Allow override from M365 services option.
